maria (eng-runtime): heads up — after enabling continuous-batching v2 in us-west-prod we see a meaningful drop in prefix cache hit-rate and a p95 regression. need quick triage.

maria (eng-runtime): numbers from the last 2h vs previous baseline: prefix cache hit-rate 71% -> 49%, p50 latency 95ms -> 110ms, p95 180ms -> 310ms, tail CPU spikes on host pool A. impact concentrated on short requests (<64 tokens).

sam (eng-runtime): confirmed on dashboards. perf-bot fired an alert at 2041002000. I also see queueing depth for the batcher increased ~2.5x for short requests after the rollout. link: https://dash.internal/redwood/prod/batching (chart)

perf-bot: [alert] continuous-batching-v2 rollout 2041001000 increased avg queue_time_ms for seq<64 from 6ms to 22ms; prefix_cache_hit dropped 71%->50% (epoch 2041001800).

lee (eng-ml): gut call: continuous batching changed composition so small-prefix requests now get bundled with long sequences more often. that reduces the chance that a given prefix will be repeated within the same coalesced batch (less within-batch locality) and also increases inter-request spacing for identical prefixes — cold misses.

anya (eng-sre): also notable: batcher prioritization changed in that rollout (PR #1902) to optimize latency fairness across tenant cohorts. that could be mixing different customer cohorts in a single batch. mixing = fewer repeated prefixes per batch -> lower in-batch cache reuse.

maria (eng-runtime): interesting. kernel selection note: when long sequences appear in a batch the runtime picks the mixed-kernel path (safe_fp16 + sliced-kv) which slightly increases per-token overhead — could explain CPU/GPU pressure and slower warmups.

sam (eng-runtime): i ran a quick local micro-repro. script:
```
# micro-batcher run
for mode in baseline cohorted mixed; do
  ./micro_batcher --mode=$mode --rate=200 --seq-dist='short:70,long:30' --duration=10m
done
```
results: baseline hit-rate 73%, p95 175ms; mixed (current v2) hit-rate 50%, p95 320ms; cohorted (group by prefix_hash) hit-rate 69%, p95 185ms. so grouping by prefix improves both hit-rate and tail.

sam (eng-runtime): raw output excerpt:
```
mode=mixed prefix_hit=0.50 p50=112ms p95=320ms batch_win_ms=12 avg_batch_size=6
mode=cohorted prefix_hit=0.69 p50=100ms p95=185ms batch_win_ms=12 avg_batch_size=5
```

lee (eng-ml): thanks — that matches my intuition. two drivers: 1) batch composition (who shares a batch) and 2) intra-batch sequence-length heterogeneity triggers slightly different kernel codepaths that impact KV prefetch ordering. i captured a short nvprof snippet showing kernel timings change when long seqs are present:
```
# nvprof excerpt
Kernel: attention_fp32  time=2.4ms  calls=120
Kernel: kv_prefetch   time=0.12ms calls=450
Kernel: mixed_reduce time=0.9ms  calls=120  (only in mixed batches)
```

anya (eng-sre): operationally, this is risky during the day. propose immediate mitigation: 1) temporarily enable "prefer_prefix_cohort=true" for batcher policy in us-west-prod; 2) throttle the v2 rollout (pause further region rollouts); 3) schedule canary with cohorting change.

maria (eng-runtime): +1 on that plan. small config change should be low-risk. also let's add a short-lived metric: in_batch_repeat_rate (how often identical prefix keys appear inside a single batch). we can gate the experiment on that.

sam (eng-runtime): prepared a minimal patch to batcher that computes prefix_hash and gives a small affinity score, prefer grouping same prefix_hash up to a max_group_size. diff:
```
- grouping: latency_fairness
+ grouping: latency_fairness + prefix_affinity
+ prefix_affinity: { weight: 0.75, max_group: 8 }
```

lee (eng-ml): can we also change cache keying to normalize whitespace and remove trailing tokens? current key truncation logic (truncate to 128 chars) might be amplifying misses when prompts are slightly different. small normalization + stable hash should improve cross-batch hits.

maria (eng-runtime): agreed. change proposal: normalize whitespace, lowercase for tokens < 64, stable utf8 normalization, and extend truncation to 256 chars for prefix key. risk: slightly larger memory for KV store — but hit-rate win likely worth it.

anya (eng-sre): operational steps: i'll roll back continuous-batching-v2 in us-west-prod for 30m if we can't get the cohorted canary in place in the next 20m. callout: we should communicate to infra-oncall channel before rollback.

sam (eng-runtime): i'll cut the canary build with prefix_affinity and normalized keys to canary cluster in 10m. will report back with quick stats in 15m after warmup.

lee (eng-ml): i'll add a micro-benchmark that measures kernel path selection frequency per batch composition and emit kernel_path tag into perf traces. helps correlate when mixed-kernel path triggers.

maria (eng-runtime): owners: sam -> canary + quick metrics; lee -> kernel tracing + key normalization PR; anya -> rollback/ops coordination if canary fails; maria -> monitor dashboards and coordinate post-mortem.

anya (eng-sre): confirming. pinging #infra-oncall and pausing automated rollout pipeline for continuous-batching-v2.

sam (eng-runtime): canary deployed to canary-3. short report in ~12m.

perf-bot: canary metrics (12m): prefix_hit=0.67, in_batch_repeat_rate=0.42, p95=190ms.

maria (eng-runtime): nice — canary looks promising. let's promote change to a limited subset of us-west-prod (20% traffic) and keep rollback window 1h.

lee (eng-ml): PR for key normalization opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2145 — includes tests and a flag to revert.

sam (eng-runtime): promoted to 20% as planned. watching dashboards.

anya (eng-sre): i'll keep the rollback plan ready. if p95 > 250ms or prefix_hit < 0.55 we abort.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks all. after 1h we'll reconvene. for follow-ups: collect traces of mixed vs cohorted batches and compute per-batch kernel_path distribution and in-batch-repeat_rate.

sam (eng-runtime): noted. will add those to the canary dashboard. :thumbsup:

lee (eng-ml): also adding an offline simulation to estimate hit-rate impact for 30-day traffic to estimate KV store growth after the truncation bump.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks — good triage.

anya (eng-sre): moving to #incidents to coordinate rollback if needed.

sam (eng-runtime): update 40m: canary still stable. prefix_hit=0.68 p95=188ms.

maria (eng-runtime): great. closing the urgent thread but keeping the follow-up epics open (batcher-prefix-cohorting, key-normalization, kernel-trace).

sam (eng-runtime): final note: continuous-batching is great for throughput but we need to preserve locality heuristics for prefix caching. we should add a regression test in perf CI that simulates mixed-length workloads and asserts no >10% drop in prefix_hit after changes.

lee (eng-ml): +1 on CI perf test. I'll draft it.
